walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit 1: Speaking — a core area of A-Level French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit 1: Speaking brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit 1: Speaking.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which auxiliary does 'se marier' take in the passé composé?
options: avoir
être
aller
faire
nuclear family
extended family
blended family
single-parent family
Either position with the same meaning.
A verb in the subjunctive mood.
An infinitive.
A noun.

mcqs.q: What does 'mes parents' mean in French?
options: It means just my mother.
It always means all my relatives.
Either position with the same meaning.
My parents (mother and father specifically) - but 'parents' can also mean relatives more broadly.

mcqs.q: Where does 'petit' usually go in relation to its noun?
options: After the noun like most French adjectives.
Before the noun (un petit garçon).
Either position with the same meaning.
It means just my mother.
